newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh says D8 bloc open to non-Islamic states.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh says D8 bloc open to non-Islamic states.

text.p: Eight developing Islamic countries in Asia and Africa are set to form an economic bloc next month, but the grouping will remain open to non-Islamic states, a Bangladesh official said on Thursday.

"We have finally decided to extend fresh membership only on the basis of consensus. So the non-Islamic states will have chances for entry," Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Abul Hasan Chowdhury told Reuters.

Bangladesh is a founding member of the Developing-8 Group (D8), which is scheduled to meet on June 15 in Turkey. Heads of states from member countries are to expected sign a declaration at the meeting to formally launch the bloc.
Other D8 sponsors are Egypt, Iran, Indonesia, Malaysia, Nigeria, Pakistan and Turkey.
Chowdhury, who represented Bangladesh in D-8 preparatory meetings, said core sponsors were chosen on the basis of population.
"Population was the basis. The most populous Islamic states had been proposed," he said.
Officials said the draft declaration had identified 30 areas, including trade, technology, transit, air links and rural development, where member states could cooperate.
"The grouping is solely aimed at expansion of trade and cooperation in other economic fields. There would be a much lower level political element," Chowdhury said.
